title: Commercialism as mental pollution; optimism
summary: Commercialism corrupts, yet he is slightly optimistic.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: We wonder why that is. A lot of it today, because we're still in such a transition here, we're conditioned to hear certain things. One of the faults we have, one of the traps that we have, is the dominance of commercialism; it really is pollution, mental pollution or indoctrination, if you like, for their own ends. It happens over and over again where they've destroyed things
without thought, to make a quick buck.
How that will work out I don't know either. It could destroy it beyond return, as they've tried to do with our rivers and maybe even stupidly with our lives, as they go through with the bomb.
If we can get through that, then maybe something--I don't know the answer. I prefer to be slightly optimistic.
I don't think we have any more ground to be pessimistic than optimistic. I think it's about even.
You're hoping in either case. One that it doesn't happen, one that it does.
Yes, most docile people try to govern their fears of what could possibly happen at its worst with hope
that people will have more sense, and sometimes they do and sometimes they don't.

Unfortunately there is that little manipulative process today that didn't exist quite to the extent that it does. When it was regional it didn't; they could manipulate within a given sphere, but not as total as it is today.
